field_semantics.filled_by: 'fetcher' = valore numerico strutturato, valutato deterministicamente. 'pending_reasoning' = testo libero, richiede lettura/interpretazione da parte di un reasoning engine.

quality_flag.IPOTESI_DI_LAVORO: Plausibile, non confermato da fonte indipendente
quality_flag.SMENTITO: Dato precedente confutato da fonte verificata

alert_level.WATCHLIST: Sotto soglia di monitoraggio ma in avvicinamento (>=70% della soglia).
alert_level.ATTIVO: Soglia di monitoraggio superata — evento rilevante confermato.
alert_level.ALLERTA_MAX: Soglia di allerta massima superata — priorità assoluta nel report.

field_semantics.threshold_triggered: true se alert_level è ATTIVO o ALLERTA_MAX.
field_semantics.tier: 1 = fonte istituzionale/primaria obbligatoria. 2 = fonte secondaria, ammessa con segnalazione esplicita.

report_construction_rules: Includere sempre: ogni evento con alert_level ATTIVO o ALLERTA_MAX, indipendentemente dall'area.
Includere: eventi pending_reasoning il cui contenuto testuale suggerisce escalation, anche senza soglia numerica — vanno letti e valutati, non scartati automaticamente.
Scartare/riassumere in una riga sola: eventi INATTIVO privi di rilevanza contestuale (es. sismicità di fondo sotto soglia, comunicati istituzionali di routine).
Collegare causalmente eventi correlati tra aree diverse quando plausibile (es. B1 geopolitica -> B6 energia -> B7 mercati) invece di elencarli come fatti isolati.
Se un record source_status riporta status 'error' per una fonte tier 1, questo VA segnalato esplicitamente in apertura di report — non va ignorato silenziosamente.
Finestra di riferimento raccomandata: rolling 48h dal timestamp extracted_at più recente nel file, salvo diversa richiesta esplicita.
In caso di dati contrastanti tra fonti, segnalare il conflitto esplicitamente invece di produrne una media o sintesi che lo nasconda.

desertification_area.note: nuova area documentata in avanzamento; soglia massima è dichiarazione UNCCD

strategic_reserves_days.note: obbligo IEA/UE: 90 giorni; sotto 60 = erosione preoccupante, sotto 30 = critica

gas_price_volatility.note: prezzo medio europeo TTF; baseline storica pre-crisi ~30€/MWh

energy_inflation_delta.note: inflazione energetica aggiuntiva rispetto a baseline OCSE/UE

vix_level.note: CBOE VIX — indice di volatilità/paura; sopra 35 storicamente coincide con fasi acute (2008, 2020)

stock_index_drawdown.note: variazione giornaliera indice azionario di riferimento (S&P 500 / DAX)

gold_price_surge.note: movimento anomalo dell'oro spot — proxy di flight-to-safety

fx_volatility.note: EUR/USD — soglie tarate su una coppia storicamente poco volatile; movimenti oltre 1.5%/giorno sono rari e segnalano stress

sovereign_spread_btp_bund.note: spread BTP-Bund 10Y; non automatizzato da fetcher (nessuna fonte gratuita stabile no-key) — valore va inserito da reasoning dopo query dedicata

industrial_rationing_signal.note: 1 = razionamento industriale formalmente annunciato o avviato da governo/ARERA/Terna

B6.name: Sicurezza Energetica e Continuita dei Servizi Essenziali
B6.note: Famiglia causale distinta da B1 (geopolitica = causa) e da B4 (cibo/acqua = altro bene essenziale). B6 monitora la continuita dei servizi energetici come bene essenziale a se stante: riserve, prezzi, segnali di razionamento industriale o civile.

B7.name: Economia e Mercati Globali
B7.note: Famiglia causale distinta da B6 (energia = bene essenziale specifico) e da B1 (geopolitica = causa politica). B7 monitora la stabilità finanziaria e monetaria come dominio a sé: mercati azionari, valute, banche centrali, debito sovrano. Spesso è EFFETTO di B1/B6 (es. shock energetico -> inflazione -> stretta monetaria) più che causa autonoma: nel report va sempre verificato il collegamento causale con le altre macro-aree attive.

content.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 400 Security Holes
content.summary: Microsoft today released updates to remedy at least 398 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software, including one weakness that is already being actively exploited and two others that were publicly detailed prior to today.

content.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
content.summary: A 26-year-old Canadian man once described as one of the most consequential cybercrime threat actors of 2024 has pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy to hack and extort more than 165 organizations that used the cloud data storage provider Snowflake. Connor Riley Moucka, of Kitchener, Ontario, also admitted to stealing call and text history records of more than 100 million AT&T customers.

content.title: Read This Before You Buy That TV Streaming Stick
content.summary: Security experts have been sounding the alarm for years about the risks of using generic TV boxes that promise unlimited content streaming for a one-time fee, warning that they secretly rent the user's Internet connection out to strangers. But a groundbreaking new analysis finds these devices also routinely spoof themselves as mobile phones clicking ads on AI-generated websites as part of sprawling operation that seeks to defraud online merchants and advertising networks.

content.title: LG to Ban Residential Proxies from Smart TV Apps
content.summary: The home appliance giant LG Electronics USA said this week it plans to suspend any apps built for its smart TVs that turn one's television into an always-on residential proxy node. The move comes less than a month after researchers found that more than 42 percent of games and other apps available for download on LG's webOS store allow unknown third-parties to route their Internet traffic through a user's TV.

content.title: Microsoft Patches a Record 570 Security Flaws
content.summary: Microsoft Corp. today released software updates to plug at least 570 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, almost triple the number of vulnerabilities the software giant fixed in its record-smashing Patch Tuesday release last month. Microsoft attributed the burgeoning patch counts to vulnerability discoveries aided by artificial intelligence.

content.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
content.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued a postmortem on a data leak in which a contractor published dozens of internal CISA credentials -- including AWS Govcloud keys -- in a public GitHub repository for almost six months before being notified by KrebsOnSecurity. Experts say the gaps identified in the agency's initial response provide important lessons that all security teams should absorb.

content.title: U.S. uranium production more than tripled in 2025 and was the highest since 2017
content.summary: In 2025, uranium concentrate production in the United States totaled 2.1 million pounds of triuranium octoxide (U3O8), the base component of nuclear reactor fuel. U.S. U3O8 production in 2025 was the most since 2017 and more than triple the volume produced in 2024.

content.title: Eight petroleum liquids pipeline projects have been completed since the start of 2025
content.summary: In the 2026 release of our Liquids Pipeline Projects Database, we tracked the completion of 8 liquid fuels pipeline projects since the start of 2025, and an additional 14 new projects have been announced.

content.title: Dangote refinery drives increase in petroleum shipments from Nigeria
content.summary: Seaborne petroleum product exports from Nigeria have grown seven-fold since 2023, playing an increasing role in the international market for petroleum products at a time when supplies from other areas have been constrained.

content.title: Longer wells boost Permian crude oil and natural gas production
content.summary: Well operators in the Permian region of western Texas and eastern New Mexico are getting more oil and gas out of the ground by drilling longer, horizontal wells and increasingly incorporating so-called super-lateral wells that exceed 15,000 feet.

content.title: Waterborne shipments from the U.S. Gulf Coast increased in April and May
content.summary: Waterborne shipments of crude oil and petroleum products from the U.S. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) to the West Coast (PADD 5) more than quadrupled year-on-year in April and May following a waiver that permitted a broader group of ships to travel between U.S. ports. Shipments from the U.S. Gulf Coast to the East Coast (PADD 1) also increased.

content.title: United States on track for record natural gas production in 2026
content.summary: We forecast U.S. marketed natural gas production will average 122.5 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) in 2026, surpassing the previous record of 118.5 Bcf/d set in 2025, in our August 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO).

content.title: Duration of power outages in Puerto Rico not caused by major events increased 19% in 2025
content.summary: In 2025, customers in Puerto Rico experienced an average of 36 hours of power interruptions that were not caused by major events such as hurricanes, 19% more than in 2024. On average, between 2021 and 2025, Puerto Rican customers experience 29 hours of power loss each year. By comparison, electricity customers in the mainland United States generally experience about two hours of electricity interruptions per year without major events.

content.title: Battery storage capacity averaged 70% growth over the last three years
content.summary: Utility-scale battery storage capacity in the United States increased significantly during the last three years, with an annual average growth rate of 70%. By the end of 2025, the U.S. power system had operational battery storage capacity of 43.6 gigawatts (GW). During the first six months of 2026, operators added another 8.3 GW of battery storage capacity, reaching nearly 52 GW of nameplate battery storage capacity, based on our latest Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory.

content.title: The U.S.-Canada natural gas and electricity trade value rose in 2025
content.summary: Although the total value of energy trade between the United States and Canada fell by 11% in 2025 to an estimated $137 billion, according to data from the U.S. Census Bureau, the trade value of natural gas and electricity between the two countries increased slightly primarily because of increased natural gas prices and trade volume.

content.title: Hourly peak load in ERCOT set a new record, exceeding 91 GW on July 22
content.summary: Hourly peak load in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), the regional transmission organization serving most of Texas, reached a record 91.1 gigawatts (GW) on July 22, 2026, according to data reported to us for our Hourly Electric Grid Monitor.
